newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Seller emerges, bids dwindle.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Seller emerges, bids dwindle.

text.p: A major finally emerged on Friday to offer gasoline after the week's dearth of sellers, but it faced only one buyer and at different levels, traders said.

Talking levels for 97-octane unleaded cargoes were mismatched with a European major's bid at $28.50 per barrel fob Singapore lifting February 18-22, higher than another European major's offer at $27.90 but for a later lifting of February 26-March 3.
Traders said although the prompt market was tight, the backwardation reflected by the bid/offer appeared too wide.
But levels moved up as 97-octane was on Thursday bid at $28.00.
The buyers for other grades disappeared but traders assessed the spread between the 97 and 95-octane at around $1.80.

Traders said India bought its third February arrival 25,000-tonne cargo of 87-octane leaded gasoline at around $2.50 per barrel over Singapore 92-octane unleaded quotes c&f Kandla/Goa. This was much lower than the last award at $4.50-$5.00 per barrel, they said.
Naphtha prices leapt by nearly $1.00 as February swaps shot up sharply to $24.85/$25.10 from the morning's level of $24.30/$24.60 and Thursday's $24.10/$24.30.
"It is a lack of selling amid a lot of buying as there is good physical demand," explained a broker.
